newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Decommissioned Russian nuclear sub sinks -agency.
newsitem.headline: Decommissioned Russian nuclear sub sinks -agency.

text.p: A 1970s vintage Russian nuclear submarine, taken out of service four years ago and stored offshore waiting to be scrapped, has sunk, Interfax news agency said on Friday.

The agency quoted sources in the Far Eastern port of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatksky as saying that the submarine sank on Thursday night. It said there was no danger. A spokeswoman for the Emergencies Ministry said she could not immediately confirm the report, but that the ministry was investigating it.

Interfax and Itar-Tass news agencies both quoted a local emergency services official as saying that the commander of the fleet had told him that the section containing the reactor was hermetically sealed and that water could not get in.
Nevertheless, he said, the ministry was carrying out radiation checks every half hour. Radiation levels were so far normal.
The agencies said the submarine sank to a depth of 18-20 metres (55-60 feet). "The active zone of the reactor had been unloaded," Interfax said.
It said the submarine hit another vessel as it was being moved. Its hull was damaged and one or two sections filled with water. Work was under way to raise the vessel by pumping in air.
